captions.instagram:
Myth: cash tips aren't income. ✂️ Stylists, barbers, nail and lash techs, this one's for you.

Fact: cash and card tips both go on your return. The new "no tax on tips" deduction works off tips you report, so skipping them can cost you the deduction.

✔️ Deduction up to $25,000 a year for tax years 2025 to 2028, with or without itemizing.
✔️ Booth renter? It can't be more than your business's net income before the deduction.
✔️ Phases out over $150,000 MAGI ($300,000 joint). Valid SSN needed; married couples file jointly.
✔️ Log tips every day, cash included.

Comment TIPS or try our no tax on tips calculator (link in bio).

Source: IRS newsroom, "What the No Tax on Tips deduction means for you"; IRS Topic 761. General information, not advice for your situation.
captions.youtube_title: Cash Tips Aren't Income? Booth Renter Myth vs Fact (No Tax on Tips)
captions.youtube_description: Myth: cash tips aren't income. Fact: cash and card tips go on your return, and the no tax on tips deduction is figured from tips you report. The deduction is up to $25,000 a year for tax years 2025 through 2028, available whether you itemize or not, needs a valid SSN, and phases out above $150,000 MAGI ($300,000 joint). For self-employed booth renters it can't exceed the net income of the business where the tips were earned. Sources: IRS newsroom; IRS Topic 761. General information, not advice for your situation.
